verdict: OK to lend selectively in Solapur home textiles — favour converters with domestic order books and clean receivables; avoid export-only towel and bedsheet mills carrying raw-material and shipment-cost stress.
title: Solapur home textiles & made-ups: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Solapur spins, weaves and converts cotton into towels, bedsheets and chaddars, selling to wholesalers, domestic brands and exporters. Capex is loom-and-processing heavy and largely fixed once installed, so a demand dip hits utilisation fast. **So when a proposal lands, check the yarn-to-receivable cycle first; if the cycle is longer than the stated credit terms, ask why inventory is being held.**

## What has changed in Solapur now
Local reporting is blunt: raw material has become expensive and orders have stopped, with the industry described as in crisis [2]. A March 2026 report puts the hit at ₹500 crore, with raw material costlier and exports disrupted, and shipment costs moving from about a thousand dollars to five thousand [3]. **This is a cost-and-order shock, not a demand collapse in the end market** — and it lands hardest on units that sell only export. Note both local reports are from 2026 and pre-date today by several months; refresh with the customer.

## The growth opportunity
Peer results point the other way. Welspun Living's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.9% to ₹2,870 crore, with home textile exports up 18.3% and domestic business up 28.2% [6]; its Q1 FY27 global B2B other products grew 32% [4]. Indo Count posted record Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹1,224 crore at 13.1% EBITDA margin [7], and Iris Clothings grew total income 40.3% YoY in Q2 FY27 [5]. **Pursue the domestic-brand and organised-retail supplier, and the converter with a mixed domestic-export book; avoid the pure export towel mill with no domestic fallback.** Maharashtra GST collections grew 8.6% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind.

## How to grow safely
Structure as cash credit against a drawing power built on paid stock and book debts, with a term loan only for proven capacity. **Take monthly stock-and-debt statements, monthly sales register, and quarterly GST returns reconciled to turnover** — the GST gap of +3.3 pp between bank credit (+15.2%) and output (+11.9%) [D] means some of this lending is running ahead of real output, so verify output, not just sales. Rating discipline: Golden Texo Fabs carries CRISIL A-/Stable on an ₹80.25 crore cash credit [9]; ICRA notes working capital is driven by inventory and receivables [10]. **If gearing or TOL/TNW drifts past the rated peer's 0.6x and 0.9x [8], ask for a fresh CMA and reduce limit.**

- GST return vs sales register (monthly): divergence above 5% -> stop fresh disbursal until reconciled. - Order book and export shipment cost (monthly): shipment cost still near the elevated level [3] -> shift exposure to domestic-order borrowers. - Receivable days (monthly): beyond stated credit terms -> ask for debtor ageing and top-five buyer confirmation. - Yarn price movement (fortnightly): sharp rise without price pass-through [2] -> review margin and drawing power.
